items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: He wrote a piece for solo trumpet that was so difficult. Oh it was so hard. And we did it in Carnegie recital hall and I was very, very nervous.

ctx.x: It just seems like another end of the spectrum for you.

I didn’t do it — it was a concert. I didn’t play with the Kronos Quartet but they opened and I did this thing. That made me nervous. That really, really made me nervous. He wrote a piece for solo trumpet that was so difficult. Oh it was so hard. And we did it in Carnegie recital hall and I was very, very nervous. I don’t know what kind of job I did. I think I could approach it with a different attitude now and do better, I really do. But it’s funny, when you’re not doing something for a while, it makes you…

playing live a lot and then all of a sudden I have to record, if I’m not in front of the recording studio microphone I get nervous in front of the recording studio microphone. If I’m playing in front of the recording studio microphone all the time it’s second nature, then you go out and play live and you get nervous if you haven’t played live in a while. But the classical thing, somehow I’ve always had a little bug about it, about like it has to be perfect.
